thread:
atlas-eng: Hey team — starting ~10:20 UTC we saw a burst of 429s and p95 token latency jumps from ~180ms -> 1.8s on our dedicated pool `atlas-prod`. This lasted ~7–10m and hit multiple routes. Opening here to get root-cause + immediate remediation.
jenna: Thanks — can you paste timestamps + example error payloads? Also pool id and whether you recently changed concurrency/quant settings?
atlas-eng: pool id `rp-atlas-03`. First seen 2027-11-02T10:19:34Z, last observed ~10:27:12Z. No config change on our side. Example response (sanitized):
```
HTTP/1.1 429 Too Many Requests
x-redwood-error: RATE_LIMIT_EXCEEDED
x-redwood-reason: pool_capacity
content-type: application/json
{
  "error": "Request rate exceeded for model: small-decoder-v2",
  "request_id": "r-0a1b2c3d"
}
```
sam: Quick check on our side — I can see periodic queue length spikes in the pool around the same window. GPU util jumped to ~96% at peaks, and the autoscaler didn't add nodes. Looking at the scaling trace there's a cooldown config set to 180s and max_nodes=5, min_nodes=3. When the burst happened we were pinned at 3 nodes and the scaling decision missed the first spike because the metric window averages smoothed it out.
marcos: Any sign of noisy-neighbor (one customer consuming disproportionate tokens) vs broad traffic increase? We can check token/s breakdown and per-tenant concurrency.
atlas-eng: We ran an internal replay for that timeframe — traffic distribution was skewed: two clients had sustained batched requests (long prompts) during the window. Baseline QPS usually ~140 r/s for atlas-prod, peak observed during campaign ~520 r/s for ~8m. Requests were larger than normal (avg 1200 tokens/request). We didn't hit per-api-key limits on our side.
jenna: That lines up — larger token sizes increase per-request GPU work. If autoscaler uses rq/s but not tokens/s or token-per-request weighting, it can under-provision. Do we have token-rate or request-workload metrics in the pool config?
sam: Current policy uses `requests_per_sec` with a simple threshold. No explicit token-weighting. Also scale cooldown is long; and max_nodes low for expected peaks. Summary from infra metrics:
- GPU util: 72% baseline -> 96% peak
- Avg queue length: 12 -> 470 at peak
- p50 token latency: 180ms -> 700ms
- p95 token latency: 1.8s -> 3.6s on worst nodes
- 429s: ~6.2% of requests during window

ops-bot: autoscaler:event - scale_decision denied (reason: max_nodes_reached)

marcos: So root causes: 1) autoscale policy tuned for r/s not tokens, 2) too-low max_nodes and conservative cooldown, 3) large prompt batch causing effective compute per-request to spike (noisy neighbor effect).

kai: Proposed immediate mitigation: bump pool max_nodes to 8 and temporarily raise headroom target so we scale earlier. Also enable token-weighted scaling if possible. Short-term we can also enable burst capacity for 30m to flatten the spike while we tune.

jenna: I propose concrete steps:
1) Temp increase max_nodes -> 8 and set min_nodes -> 4 for next 2 hours (ops apply at 11:00 UTC) to drain queue.
2) Reduce scale_cooldown from 180s -> 30s to react faster.
3) Add token-weighting in autoscaler (weight = avg_tokens_per_request) — requires infra change, schedule for next deploy.
4) Recommend pool utilization target of 60% (instead of current 80%) for production pools with heavy long requests; document this in capacity playbook.

sam: Adding a suggested config snippet to apply quickly:
```
{
  "pool": "rp-atlas-03",
  "min_nodes": 4,
  "max_nodes": 8,
  "scale_cooldown_secs": 30,
  "scale_strategy": "weighted_tokens",
  "utilization_target": 0.6,
  "burst_capacity": {"enabled": true, "duration_secs": 1800}
}
```
atlas-eng: Please go ahead with the temporary bump. Also request that we get a post-mortem with suggested quota/guardrails so this doesn't recur. We can also throttle the two heavy clients temporarily if needed — I can coordinate with their teams.

jenna: Ops — can you approve the quick change and confirm once applied? We should also capture a snapshot of metrics + logs for the window for the post-mortem.

marcos: I'll run a shorter reproducible load test against atlas-prod to validate scaling changes. Test plan:
- baseline: 150 r/s, avg 400 tokens
- spike: 600 r/s, avg 1200 tokens for 10m
- measure: p95 latency, queue length, scale ops

sam: One more follow-up: We should add a per-key concurrency cap (e.g., 12 concurrent requests) and a soft token-rate guard for the pool to prevent single clients from saturating compute. Will draft guardrail PR.

ops-bot: deploy:pool-config-change - applied by ops @2027-11-02T11:02:15Z to rp-atlas-03 (min_nodes=4,max_nodes=8,scale_cooldown=30s,burst=1800s)

jenna: Thanks — after ops applied config we saw queue drain within ~2m and 429s drop to <0.1%. Need to monitor the next 24h. Atlas-eng, we'll schedule a capacity review next week to set new steady-state commits and recommended utilization targets.

atlas-eng: Confirmed — queue normalized and p95 back to ~220ms. Thanks all. Please include recommended reserve headroom in the follow-up doc (we favor ~30% reserved for bursts).

kai: Actions and owners:
- ops: temp config change applied (done) -> ops
- sam: PR for token-weighted scaling + per-key guards -> in progress
- marcos: run reproducibility test and share results -> owner
- jenna: schedule capacity planning call with Atlas next week -> owner

jenna: Closing thread for now, will re-open if we see regression. :thumbsup:
